newsitem.title: PERU: Cambior seeks electricity supply for Peru project.
newsitem.headline: Cambior seeks electricity supply for Peru project.

text.p: Canada's Cambior Inc has invited firms to pre-qualify to bid for a contract to supply the miner with a capacity of 125 megawatts (MW) of electricity for its La Granja copper project in Peru, a company official said Tuesday.
Firms had until October 28 to present their credentials to pre-qualify for the bidding, La Granja projects manager, Jorge Lanza, said in an interview.
Lanza said the first electricity supply from the winning bidder would be in 1997 and would gradually increase to the desired capacity of 125 MW.
The energy supply could come from a firm's existing capacity or from the construction of a new electricity plant, he added.
"There are various foreign and Peruvian companies interested in building an electricity plant," Lanza said. "It would be a plant that gradually increased the supply of energy for our operations."
Cambior is looking for a partner to help finance its planned $800 million project to produce 250,000 tonnes of copper in concentrate at 57 cents a pound from 2001, company officials have said.

In May, the company said La Granja held mineable reserves of 720.6 million tonnes graded at 0.69 percent copper. Including possible reserves and using a cut-off grade of 0.4 percent copper, Cambior calculated the site held 3.74 billion tonnes of ore.
The firm acquired a five-year option on 100 percent of the property from state-run Minero Peru S.A. in March 1994, promising to spend $25 million on exploration.
Cambior hopes to complete its feasibility by early 1997.

La Granja, located in the Cajamarca department some 400 miles (640 kms) north of Lima, was billed originally as a copper-gold site but does not have enough gold to mine economically, officials have said.
